height_mm.conditions: YZP0015 overall height from seating plane, '0.5 MAX'

v_in_min.conditions: RX_SUP receiver supply, Recommended Operating Conditions. Three separate rails: RX_SUP 2-3.6 V, IO_SUP 1.7 V to min(3.6, RX_SUP), TX_SUP 3.0-5.25 V.

v_in_max.conditions: TX_SUP transmitter supply, Recommended Operating Conditions (the highest of the three rails; RX_SUP maxes at 3.6 V)

i_quiescent.conditions: RX_SUP current in hardware power-down (PWDN) mode, external clock mode with the external clock switched off (IO_SUP 3 uA, TX_SUP 2 uA in the same state)

i_typ.conditions: RX_SUP current, normal operation in dynamic power-down mode (dynamic power-down 90% / active 10% of the period); TX_SUP = 4 V, RX_SUP = IO_SUP = 3 V, 100-Hz PRF. Excludes LED drive current.

i_max.conditions: Peak LED drive current sourced through TX_SUP in 100-mA LED current mode (ILED_2X = 1); 50 mA in the default ILED_2X = 0 mode. Pulsed, limited to 3% cumulative duty cycle at 100 mA and 10% at 50 mA by the Absolute Maximum Ratings.

source.section: 7.5 Electrical Characteristics -- TRANSMITTER, LED current range

theta_ja.conditions: YZP (DSBGA) 15 balls, junction-to-ambient thermal resistance per TI thermal metrics (JEDEC standard board)

variables.v_tx_sup: TX_SUP rail voltage, 3.0 V to 5.25 V -- a design choice set by the LED forward drop (TX_SUP must be at least 0.5 + VLED in 50-mA mode, 1.0 + VLED in 100-mA mode)
variables.i_led: Programmed LED current, 0-50 mA (ILED_2X = 0) or 0-100 mA (ILED_2X = 1), 6-bit programmable -- a design choice, not a part property
variables.led_duty_cycle: Cumulative sum of all LED phase durations over the total period; the Absolute Maximum Ratings cap this at 10% in 50-mA mode and 3% in 100-mA mode

source.section: 7.1 Absolute Maximum Ratings / 7.3 Recommended Operating Conditions

f_fundamental_hz.conditions: Pulse repetition frequency (PRF), the rate at which the LED phases fire. Programmable 10 SPS to 1000 SPS; 100-Hz PRF is the datasheet's Electrical Characteristics test condition. Each pulse steps the TX_SUP current between ~0 and the programmed LED current (up to 50 or 100 mA).
Internal oscillator frequency, 4 MHz, +/-1% accuracy at room temperature. In external clock mode the input clock may be 4 MHz to 60 MHz instead.

t_op_min.conditions: Operating temperature range, Recommended Operating Conditions. Note this is a narrower range than most of the BOM (-20 C, not -40 C).

t_op_max.conditions: Operating temperature range, Recommended Operating Conditions

conducted.reason: PPG receive chain passband. The switched-RC filter after the transimpedance amplifier has a 2.5-kHz bandwidth (which scales down with sampling duty cycle -- roughly 50 Hz at a 2% sampling width). The photodiode input nets INP/INN are the vulnerable nodes; anything conducted into them inside this band lands directly on the heart-rate signal.

noise_floor.conditions: Receiver SNR over a 20-Hz bandwidth, 500-kOhm gain setting, 50% FS output, 2% LED and sampling pulse duration, ADC averages = 16. dBFS refers to a 2-V full scale, so this is an SNR figure, not an absolute input-referred noise voltage.

design_notes.note: TX1, TX2 and TX3 are fast-switching LED drive lines and must be routed away from the sensitive INP/INN photodiode inputs. This is the device's own primary layout rule: the AFE is simultaneously the noise source and the victim, so the two net classes must be physically separated on the board.

The device draws high switching currents from the TX_SUP pin; a decoupling capacitor must be electrically close to that pin. The LED pulse is a hard load transient on TX_SUP, so the loop area between the cap, the pin, and the LED return must be minimised.

Ambient light adds to the LED-phase output because it reaches the photodiode the same way LED light does. Ambient subtraction only cancels it if the effect on the LED and ambient phases is equal; any periodic modulation of ambient light produces spurious tones in the (LED-Ambient) data. Keep t1 (start of LED to start of sampling) above 25 us, prevent any phase output from saturating the TIA, and minimise the spacing between LED and ambient sampling instants.

source.section: 9.2.2.2 Reducing Sensitivity to Ambient Light Modulation

design_notes.note: TIA output saturation disturbs the photodiode bias, and the recovery transient can span into the following phases -- e.g. saturation in the LED3 phase can corrupt both LED1 and Ambient1. Every phase must be kept out of saturation by periodic gain adjustment, even phases whose data the heart-rate algorithm ignores.

source.section: 9.2.2.2 Reducing Sensitivity to Ambient Light Modulation

design_notes.note: Supply sequencing is prescribed: RX_SUP first, then IO_SUP, then TX_SUP, then release RESETZ, before any I2C device settings are written. A power tree that brings TX_SUP up before RX_SUP violates the documented sequence.

provenance.notes: Only one package is offered (YZP DSBGA, 15 balls), so theta_ja has a single entry. No junction-temperature limit is published -- the Absolute Maximum Ratings table lists storage temperature (-60 to 150 C) but no TJ max -- so t_junction_max is deliberately absent. No dissipation number is given either; the dissipation_model is marked 'assumed' because the datasheet states the LED current range, the TX_SUP range and the duty-cycle limits but never writes the product as a dissipation formula, so the expression is our composition of those three stated facts and must be reviewed as such. No radiated-emissions entry: no intentional transmitter (the 'transmitter' here is an LED driver, an optical source, not RF). susceptibility.conducted noise_floor is recorded as the datasheet's receiver SNR in dBFS because TI publishes no input-referred current or voltage noise density for this part.
